thread:
sasha: heads up — running into a weird SSL verification failure when using the Python SDK against a Dedicated cluster behind our customer proxy. works fine without proxy.

sasha: gist of setup:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(
    base_url=\"https://dedicated.example.internal\",
    api_key=MY_KEY,
    proxies={\"https\": \"http://10.0.0.1:3128\"},
    ca_bundle=\"/etc/pki/custom_chain.pem\"  # custom CA chain with intermediate + root
)
resp = client.chat.create(
    model=\"gptx-small\",
    input=\"hello\"
)
```

sasha: error is a requests SSLError: \"certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate\" when the proxy does a CONNECT. works if I set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/pki/custom_chain.pem and remove client.ca_bundle argument.

leo: can you paste the full stack trace? curious if it's failing inside urllib3/requests or in our TLS wrapper. also which python-requests version?

sasha: stack trace (trimmed):
``
requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='dedicated.example.internal', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/chat (Caused by SSLError(\"certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1129)\"))
  File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/requests/sessions.py\", line 646, in send
    r = adapter.send(request, **kwargs)
``
python-requests 2.31.0, urllib3 2.0.4

maya: are you using our async client or sync? we have slightly different session plumbing between them.

sasha: sync for now. async shows slightly different behavior but also fails in a different place (ssl.SSLCertVerificationError).

maya: interesting: REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env var wins because requests builds its own SSLContext from env at import/time of creating session. our client code currently passes `verify` path into `requests.Session` only for some code paths — looks like proxy CONNECT path ends up delegating to urllib3's PoolManager which may not get our explicit verify if we aren't creating the pool with that context.

ron: this rings a bell — dedicated deployments often have corporate proxies that intercept TLS. If the proxy returns its cert chain, requests needs to trust the proxy CA too. combining certs into a single file and pointing REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is a pragmatic workaround.

leo: workaround summary that worked for me locally: 1) cat intermediate.pem root.pem > /tmp/combined.pem 2) export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/tmp/combined.pem 3) remove ca_bundle arg from client and restart app. confirmed requests+CONNECT uses env path.

sasha: confirmed, that workaround makes it go green. but it's surprising because SDK docs suggested passing ca_bundle to client if you have custom certs.

maya: yep — bug. SDK accepts ca_bundle param (typing: Optional[str]) and stores it but we don't always propagate it into the urllib3 pool when proxies are present. also the async client typing uses `ca_bundle: Union[str, List[str]]` in one place in stubs which is inconsistent.

maya: proposed short-term actions:
- add clear docs note about REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE + proxies for Dedicated/private deployments
- fix code path so that when ca_bundle is provided we construct an SSLContext and pass it into urllib3/requests poolmanager used for proxied connections
- unify typing for ca_bundle to be Optional[str] and accept a single path (list-of-paths can be documented as a concatenation step)

leo: agree. I'll open a quick PR for the typing + unit test that reproduces the proxied CONNECT case (mocked). maya, can you add an integration test on our CI image that uses a tiny mitm proxy container?

maya: yes. I can add a smoke integration that runs in dev CI (not default) and a docs snippet showing the env var workaround.

sasha: small follow-up: when ca_bundle is a path we also set verify=True in requests API — but if someone passes a cert bundle bytes or multiple files that's awkward. I'd prefer doc guidance: concat to single PE M file first.

ron: also check TLS versions: some proxies downgrade to TLSv1.2 and our runtime complains about cipher suites. but that's orthogonal.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: devex/patch-proxy-ca (branch: fix/proxy-ca) — runbook auto-triggered.

leo: ok created https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/842 (draft) — adds explicit SSLContext creation and passes it to urllib3 PoolManager for proxied flows + fixes typing. tests included.

sasha: tested the patch locally — fixes the issue for me (both with ca_bundle arg and with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env). thanks!

maya: I'll add docs to the dedicated/private setup guide and include sample docker-compose showing how to create /etc/ssl/certs/custom.pem from customer-provided files.

leo: leaving a short TODO: create an example repo under examples/py/dedicated-proxy-ca that demonstrates env var, client arg, and concat workflow.

sasha: final note — we should surface this in onboarding checklist for customer success: \"if dedicated clusters sit behind customer proxies you must provide concatenated CA chain and either set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or pass ca_bundle and restart app; see examples\"

maya: agreed. filing a doc ticket after PR merges.

ron: thanks team, marking as resolved in thread — reopen if customer hits again. :thumbsup:
